answer: Rewards can be tied to survival rather than registration. A key earns nothing at birth: payouts unlock only after it has answered several consecutive epochs and cleared peer grading. Reputation grows like a garden, slowly and under observation, so a farm of fresh keys holds assets yielding nothing until they age. Auditors wander the pool at random, so clusters of young keys submitting near-identical text are pruned before maturing. Forfeited bonds then become the nectar that pays honest reviewers. An attacker must pay to register, wait to earn, and risk losing a whole cohort at once.
